doc.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

title: Musicians' responsibility to the audience; saving Part Two
summary: Musicians' exclusivity and failure to explain; they agree to revisit in Part Two.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: But they’re not really coalescing here but somehow, so when I say there’s nothing to understand about jazz, so then you have some responsibility also on the part of the musicians. Now a musician might say, a jazz musician might say, when Vladimir Horowitz comes out to play, or the Juilliard String Quartet, they don’t go to the microphone and say, I hope you like this little tune by Schubert, you know when he wrote it I have a funny story about it and all that kind of — so they just play. But by mimicking the behavior or not necessarily explaining what they’re doing to the audience, or acting in a way that kind of projects an exclusivity or non-inclusion, or being too hip for the room, then you start to get kind of masochistic people who actually enjoy being treated either rudely or curtly by a band. And it’s all complicated. And I actually don’t have the answer but I can just throw out these various observations and maybe someone — if I thought about it I could kind of make it cohesive.
When we do Part Two of this interview, we’ll reflect on that.
Lot of food for thought there.
